items.title: You don't have to let AI think for you
items.pt:
You can open an LLM, describe a problem, and have a plausible answer before you've finished thinking about it. It can draft an email, explain a concept, suggest a fix for a bug, or give you a plan for a difficult conversation.

That's useful. It's also a little strange. When an answer is always a prompt away, it's easy to reach for one before you've had a chance to decide what you think.

items.title: What can happen after a payment platform already received your payout
items.pt:
A factual account of a USD 330 hold, what freelancers can do next, and why I built a small awareness site with open comments.

I did not expect a payout to stay held after the platform had already said it received the money.

On 13 November 2026, Skydo marked a payment of USD 330 as received, and wrote that I should expect settlement by 16 November. Nothing had been asked for before that receipt. Then came a document loop, the expected date moved to 17 November, and the funds were still held.

items.title: Hourly to Salary Conversion: The Math Behind Pay Transparency
items.pt:
Hourly to Salary Conversion: The Math Behind Pay Transparency


"$25 an hour" sounds simple. It is not. The same hourly rate can mean a $52,000 salary or a $45,000 one, depending on how many hours you actually work, whether you get paid holidays, and what overtime does to the picture. items.title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
items.pt: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) can operate directly on the parameters of other neural networks. They can read what a network was trained to do, fix a network that fails, and write working networks from scratch, all without gradient descent. This capability has been termed Weight-Space Programming (WSP). Exploring this new paradigm systematically requires a robust benchmark. We introduce WEIGHTBENCH, a benchmark that evaluates LLMs of increasing capability on 42 WSP tasks acr
